A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReflectiVA study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and VQA evaluations, ablations, token-prediction accuracies, and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-4/GPT-4V comparisons and two ablation variants.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, four reflective tokens, two-stage training procedure, losses, and retrieval/generation pipeline remain unchanged. The new single-model and Contriever variants are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained, including Encyclopedic-VQA, InfoSeek, LLaVA-Instruct, ViQuAE, S3VQA, and the standard MLLM/VQA benchmarks. ViQuAE/S3VQA results move from v1 Table 6 to v2 Appendix Table 9; they are not new evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-4 and GPT-4V as evaluated comparators for answer accuracy in Table 2 and reflective-token prediction in Table 11. Their earlier use for annotation or judging did not constitute these comparisons. The existing retrieval-augmented comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New Table 5 controls train a single model using full-dataset LLaMA-3.1 annotations and replace relevance-token selection with Contriever's top-2 passages, using five retrieved documents. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and settings remain unchanged. The newly stated validation-based stopping rule is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed training protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 5 add targeted tests of two-stage training against a single-model alternative and learned relevance assessment against Contriever selection. These extend the existing first-stage-only and random-passage controls. The previous sensitivity analyses, re-ranking studies, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing scores are retained. Table 5 newly reports 30.7/28.5 for the LLaMA-annotated single-model control and 29.3/29.9 for Contriever selection, measured on E-VQA single-hop/InfoSeek overall, versus the unchanged ReflectiVA scores of 35.5/40.1. Tables 2 and 11 also add GPT-4/GPT-4V answer and token-prediction results. These are additional results, not improvements between versions under the same setting.

T1.justification: The task and database definitions, equations (1)–(7), and Appendix C.2's probability-based ranking formulation are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: token-guided multimodal retrieval, two-stage training, improved knowledge-based VQA, and preservation of general multimodal capabilities. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 extends its interpretation to argue that full-dataset LLaMA-3.1 annotations do not match the proposed training strategy and that explicit relevance modeling outperforms direct Contriever passage selection. The applicability discussion and Appendix E limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that training stops according to loss on a separate validation split extracted from training data. It also clarifies that Encyclopedic-VQA question-answer pairs can have up to five images and changes the code/model access pointer from the repository to a project page. These disclosures do not establish changed underlying experiments or resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the GPT-4 technical report and LLaVA-MORE. The related-work narrative and positioning against Wiki-LLaVA, RORA-VLM, EchoSight, and Self-RAG otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits expand experimental explanations and acknowledgments and move the zero-shot generalization discussion from Section 4.3 into Appendix C.1. Most prose, the method exposition, and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 5, and 11 gain rows, and Tables 2–3 replace gray labeling of incomparable results with dagger markers. The zero-shot table moves into the appendix, Table 12 shifts position, and the unchanged failure-case figure moves to the end as Figure 7. These are localized display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: v2 tests its central design choices more convincingly: Table 5 adds a Contriever alternative to v1's random-passage control and a single-model training alternative. GPT-4/GPT-4V comparisons provide stronger reference points, while the stopping-rule disclosure improves transparency. These targeted gains strengthen empirical support; the method, coverage, principal results, and limitations remain largely unchanged.
